summary: Task 9 passes the CLI and API contract delta at HEAD 53cc3ada. The new shared seam decodedAnswerFindings closes RB3-01 and RA4-01 for the caller. Both providers refuse before any review file, raw copy, success entry, or result log. Both decoded refusals end with the exact contract suffix. Safe answers keep the reported model, the model source, and the raw bytes. The exit codes and the manifest and evidence shapes are unchanged from cf5743b7. RC4-1 is closed. Four nonblocking findings remain: an unbounded recursive walker, a quadratic cost on the record path, asymmetric raw-byte refusal text, and a dead export of the weaker check.
contract_applicability: applicable. The strategy names the task 9 CLI and API surface, and the phase diff changes the two provider refusal paths and the caller-visible refusal text in src/storytime/book-pictures.ts. contract.md:291-304 states the refusal, suffix, redaction, model, and byte rules that the diff must hold.
rc4_1_status: closed. Both decoded refusals now end with the exact suffix 'the raw answer is refused; no review or raw copy is written.' The MiniMax message is at book-pictures.ts:3344-3345 and the Kimi message is at book-pictures.ts:3668-3669.
nonblocking_findings: RC5-1 (nonblocking, medium): the shared walker decodedAnswerFindings recurses without a depth bound (src/storytime/book-pictures.ts:1174-1191). The walk function calls itself at line 1189 for every nested value. A deeply nested answer raises RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded inside the walk. The answer is still refused before any write, so no credential reaches evidence. The caller receives 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' with no pattern name and no contract suffix. contract.md:293-295 asks the walker to traverse every depth, and test-strategy.md:625 forbids a depth limit. A follow-up task should replace the recursion with an explicit worklist.

RC5-2 (nonblocking, medium): the new check raises the cost of the provider record path. jsonObjects re-extracts every nested object from the raw text, and the walker visits each copy again. secretFindings rebuilds the environment credential rules on every key. One decodedAnswerFindings call on a nested answer took 264 ms at depth 50, 935 ms at depth 100, 3.6 s at depth 200, 14.3 s at depth 400, and 60.5 s at depth 800 on a 4.8 KB answer. The Kimi --raw file allows 65,536 bytes. The operator waits with no output. A follow-up task should build the credential rules once per call and visit each extracted object once.

RC5-3 (nonblocking, low): the raw-byte refusal messages keep the asymmetry that RC4-1 reported for the decoded messages. MiniMax says 'The provider output matched credential pattern X; the raw answer is refused and nothing is written.' (book-pictures.ts:3334-3336). Kimi says 'The raw answer matched credential pattern X; nothing is written.' (book-pictures.ts:3657-3659). The MiniMax path appends a sanitized failure ledger entry through runPaidCall (book-pictures.ts:1046-1054), so 'nothing is written' overstates the outcome there. The text is unchanged from cf5743b7, and contract.md:299 fixes the decoded-refusal suffix only. A caller that matches on message text still sees two shapes.

RC5-4 (nonblocking, low): decodedReviewFindings (book-pictures.ts:1151) now has no caller in src, scripts, or tests. The plan requires only that production acceptance does not depend on it, and the diff confirms that. The dead export is the weaker named-field check, so a future caller could use it by mistake. A follow-up task should delete it or mark it as not for production use.

The check is a superset of the old named-field check. parseModelReview selects its review from the same jsonObjects extraction (line 1100), and decodedAnswerFindings walks that same extraction (line 1192). Every persisted decoded field, the reason, the issues, the count keys, and the reported model, comes from an object the walker visits.

handoff: The phase 2 task 9 CLI and API contract holds at HEAD 53cc3ada. No blocking finding. No question blocks this handoff. The raw-byte refusal text stays as is because it is unchanged from cf5743b7 and contract.md:299 fixes the decoded-refusal suffix only. UX browser review does not apply because the task changes no UI.
